passages.note: Ortiz is listed as a co-sponsor of HB2721, a middle-housing zoning bill, on the bill's status page.

passages.provision_quote: On or before January 1, 2026, a municipality with a population of seventy-five thousand persons or more must authorize by ordinance and incorporate into its development regulations, zoning regulations and other official controls the development of duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes and townhomes as a permitted use on both of the following:
passages.note: HB2721's enacted text requires cities to permit middle housing by right and bars several zoning restrictions on it, a deregulation pattern the housing annex treats as on-question but direction-only.
The House Final Reading vote detail shows Ortiz voted Y on HB2721's passage, 42-15-3-0-0.

rows.reasoning: Ortiz co-sponsored HB2721 (2024) and voted Y on its House Final Reading passage, 42-15-3-0-0. HB2721 requires municipalities to permit middle housing by right and bars several zoning restrictions on it, which the housing annex treats as on-question for 'cut the regulations and zoning limits that block private building' but only direction-only, since one deregulation law cannot show the rung's 'at most' ceiling.
